u01-open.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. μνήμην ἐποιήσω and ἐπεσκέψω are aorist middle 2nd person singular ('you remembered … you looked after'), addressed to God as in Ps 8:5, so the English is right. 'For having been heard before, he says, I ask to be heard now as well' is in the Greek (Καὶ πρότερον γὰρ εἰσακουσθείς, φησίν, … καὶ νῦν εἰσακουσθῆναι δέομαι); the flag came from a chunk boundary. Psalm 108 [109]:18 is the curse spoken against Judas (κατὰ τὸ λεγόμενον ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἰουδᾶ) and Isaiah 66:18 is right; the 'Ps 32,6' and similar headings are the edition's lemmata. 'Not yet a house of God had been built', 'the new worship of God' (θεοσέβεια), 'altogether small' and the participle points are style.

u01-open.resolution: I found no meaning error. ἐποιήσω is 2nd person singular aorist middle ('you made'), not 1st person, so 'you remembered him' is correct. The sentence about having been heard before is present in the Greek (εἰσακουσθείς … εἰσακουσθῆναι δέομαι). Psalm 108 [109]:18 identifies the verse said of Judas. 'Worship of God' for θεοσέβεια and 'I have asked' for ἐζήτησα are acceptable renderings.
